It has been OK at least since the fifties.

My memories go back to the 1950's, and when I was young it was customary in introductions to use the first and last name, and then it was up to the person being introduced to supply permission for the use of the first name. "Call me Al." But that formality does seem to have slipped away, I know I often forget names both first and last when I'm introduced and I try to use them a few times to get them to stick; so I suppose I've been part of that erosion.

Also there's a current trend to introduce people with only their first name, and that person will supply you with the last name as a distance-closer.

As a child of that time, I still can't feel comfortable addressing people in businesses who are identified by first-name tags. It seems forward, too informal to me. I feel better if I introduce myself by my first name; then I can use theirs. Mostly I just don't.
